The test image shows a split corn stalk with darkened/black internal pith tissue and shredded vascular bundles. The interior is dark gray-black, suggesting stalk rot. Top candidates: Charcoal_Stalk_Rot (black pith with microsclerotia), Diplodia_Stalk_Rot (shredded straw-colored pith), Gibberella_Disease (pink-red interior), Fusarium_Disease.

Now viewing one reference from each top candidate:
Good match - dark gray-black pith, shredded vascular bundles, white particles visible. Now checking Diplodia_Stalk_Rot:
Diplodia shows straw-colored dry stalk - lighter than test image. Now checking Gibberella_Disease:
Gibberella shows ear rot - not a match. Need one more class view. Checking Fusarium_Disease:

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Split corn stalk showing dark gray-black internal pith, shredded/fibrous vascular bundles, small white particles visible - classic stalk rot cross-section
- **Charcoal_Stalk_Rot ref**: Near-identical match - same dark gray-black pith, shredded tissue, white microsclerotia dots
- **Diplodia_Stalk_Rot ref**: Straw-colored collapsed stalk - too light, not matching
- **Gibberella_Disease ref**: Ear rot with pink mold on kernels - completely different
- **Fusarium_Disease ref**: Ear rot on kernels - completely different

The dark/black discoloration of pith with shredded vascular tissue and visible white microsclerotia is the hallmark of Charcoal Stalk Rot (*Macrophomina phaseolina*).
